claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily reliant on RNG during training and races, where a well-prepared character can still lose due to unpredictable race positioning or random training outcomes.

citations.review_text:
Its a beautiful game with a wonderful premise, fun writing, a lovely art style, iconic character design, and a fictional lore that references many real race horses in an endearing way.

Sadly, the gameplay stops being fun when you hit a grind wall that depends almost entirely on grinding against sadistic RNG. Overprepared your precious Uma for a race with all the right stats and skills to defeat the competition? Too bad. The game boxed her into the herd for the entire race like a prison, and no amount of Power or Skills can break her out; especially if she just decides to be dumb and not use her skills.

It has been impossible for me to train an Uma above A+ as of 55 hours in, and appears to be nearly impossible for the upcoming 500 hours even with guides. While I appreciate the game's community and eagerness to teach other players, the best they can do is improve on how you gamble your precious time or money on this game.

The gameplay loops eventually make you numb to the characters you used to care about because you keep failing to make any progress in this game if you are free-to-play, and I wish the developer had emphasized cosmetics instead of pay-to-win banner characters in their monetization of this game.

, however it is grindy and repetitive to no bounds , also alot UMAs require atleast 4-5 copies to be good and are time limited so theres a big FOMO element to the gacha , the gameplay is incredibly boring you just go open the same exact story mode and keep pressing the training button with almost no change and hoping for good results over and over and over and over again until you finally get a run where you end up with good stats and sparks and then take her to online where things still suck because this is a gacha game and there's always a bigger whale ... which ALSO doesn't matter because alot of these races are random as all heck and sometimes your horse will just decide that they don't feel like winning and wing it at the back of the race and never break through the pack , even though she has a crap ton of force

1- congratulations you will love this game
2- i think you might have a problem , but that's not my problem so uh play the game ig

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that skip options for events lack a proper middle-ground speed or have encounter skip settings enabled by default that cause players to miss dialogue.

citations.review_text:
You will hate this game, you will love this game. You will say "its so over" followed by "we are so back".

I really like this game for its storylines mostly, gachas tend to pass me by for the slop factories they are. But something about this game in particular, especially with real life horse racing and their counterparts and stories, sucks me in. I gave it a 8 hour trial run, i have now 46 hours and i realize im gonna be in deeper. Still a F2P and i intend to keep it that way (this game REALLY tempts you, don't fall for it). 

The gameplay is also pretty fun, and each character not only having their own specially crafted events + quirks you have to learn about them to maximize a character to the fullest potential, make loops much more interesting. (and a Independent Training mode too so you can set and forget for storylines you already completed). I really like overcoming the odds, I really like that there is a good level of depth and thought put into every card event in this game even if there are one off gags and whatnot. It also makes you want to mix and match to see what happens. 

My two major criticisms that are related to one part of the game im really not a fan of. Skips. Skip speed is either slow as molassas or way too fast, so you can't just kick back and read things at a brisk speed unless you mash, there needs to be a middle ground. Also, Skip First-Ecnounter events being ON by default is a absolute sin and can cause you to miss dialogue you didn't mean to zoom past. If you play this game, set that to OFF. 

A gacha that actually made me stick around, not bad at all Cygames.

This game is phenomenal inside and out. I'm not really one for gacha games after Dragon Ball Legends burning me out, but Umamusume is one of very few gacha games that I would advocate for.

The story of the game uses a visual novel style, and it's done really well. The animations keep from the characters feeling stiff while talking, and the cutscenes in between dialogue are pretty lively. If you're playing with the 'auto' option enabled, it almost feels as if you're watching an anime in sub. I haven't watched the actual anime, but I may not need to if I keep getting characters to unlock and play the stories of.

Speaking of, there's the Career mode. There are 3 scenarios in which you can play through a character's story--think of it as a separate story from your character's story that happens in parallel. There are also support cards you can equip before a Career that influence specific events and actions during the career--you can think of these as side quests that give extra rewards. You train your character throughout turns to reach a specific goal (e.g. 9,000 fans, top 3 in a race, etc.) with story events and side quests throughout. I recommend not using Quick Mode for a first time playthrough if you're wanting to experience a character's story.

The music is also pretty great if you're into anime J-Pop idol music. Even if you're not, it's still hard to deny the sheer quality--and quantity--of the music in this game. Mejiro McQueen's concert song in the story comes to mind immediately when I think of quality. There was also a song for Biwa Hayahide's Rouge Caroler outfit called 'Christmaspecial' that's sung in English, and it's performance is beautiful in my- well, ears.

I know there's a lot more that I'm missing, but this review would be *way* too long, so I'm going to cut things short: Try the game if you're interested.

Do note: The game installs ~10-11GB of data to a folder in AppData. So, if you don't want it to take up valuable space on your C:/ drive lik…

citations.review_text:
*I've played since the game's 0.5 anniversery so my stats on here do not line up with my real stats

Umamusume is a very fun gatcha game HOWEVER, it is one of the more intense gatcha out there. Carats (the pull currency for both their support cards and umas) are quite far and few between while also requiring significant amount of them to get effective support cards, so you need to be stratigic on what you skip and what you go for. the training is also quite luck base but again, it a gatcha so you should be expecting this

Now with all this negativity above, why have I still recommend this game? Well, the gameplay loop is really enjoyable as well as being able to see that the devs really care about it with constant events, griping storys that match with the IRL horses, and constant refreshers with new senarios. But it important to understand what you are getting yourself into, this game isn't for everyone, and that ok, you can still appreciate the time and care that the devs have put into it without playing it. 

This game is only a small part of the wider Umamusume franchise, if you don't want to play it but experiance the universe you can watch the anime or play Umamusme: Party Dash (tho from what I've heard it isn't the greatest but hey you may enjoy it.)

Overall rating: 9/10.
Great game but you need to prepare yourself before entering.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Longtime players praise the fully rendered character stories while grappling with harsh banner pities and competitive disadvantages for free players.

claims.claim: The game features an accelerated schedule on the global version which leaves little breathing room between PvP events and provides increased daily currency.

citations.review_text: Just another game you'll wish you could quit but can't bring yourself to (victim of the sunk cost fallacy). Accellerated timeline on global leaves little breathing room between PVP events. You CAN have fun without following the meta as it can be experimental and there is a lot of wiggleroom for constructing your own builds to counter / compete, however whales have a massive advantage due to how the pull system works. ON THAT NOTE, incredibly unforgiving, nothing carries over between pulls, it's a fresh start everytime. That being said, F2P players can enjoy a lot of story and the gameplay loop can be incredibly addictive and rewarding IF YOU HAVE THE TIME FOR IT, currently it takes me 2-3 hours to do all three of the career runs you're given per day. That being said, I will continue playing. You have been warned.

Umamusume is secretly an excel spreadsheet simulator disguised as an epic horse girl racing simulator. 10% of the game is watching the fruits of your labor in champions meetings and the other 90% is spent behind the scenes. You're planning, calculating the ideal parents, sparks, parents, grandparents, etc. etc. It does get sweaty especially if you're pushing for Group A finals, but there's fun in competition. That's the fun to this game. You decide how deep you want to jump into the rabbit hole of this game's systems. 

Gacha-wise, the pull economy has improved to 75 carats a day due to our accelerated schedule. Just be sure to save your carats and pull tickets for an uma or support card you really want because some bring more value than others. It's typical powercreep stuff. Hard pity is 200 and there is no carry over onto other banners. There are many community resources to help plan out your carat spending plan. It's a gacha, so expect spenders to have the edge in Champions Meetings. But even then, that's not the end of the world if you don't place well. With careful planning, you can likely together a strong account without spending a penny (I only say likely because gacha is gacha.)

But even if that's not your cup of tea, there's a lot of story to unpack with the main stories with fully rendered 3-D models and an immersive storytelling experience. They also run side events which also give good resources. With the independent training out, doing your dailies and reaching event point milestones has never been easier.

I would recommend the game to casual players who enjoy VN and interesting characters. They did a good job with the story and the accelerated schedule is a huge plus since there is always something new.

However

The game is very predatory. You either spend hundreds of dollars for ONE fully unlocked card or you spend months saving free currency, skipping every single banner. The pity system is brutal, the RNG is brutal, and you can spend dozens of hours or even days and weeks grinding with 0 progress to your account. The game forces you to grind more and more for incremental gains if you're lucky just to MAYBE win the monthly pvp mode. It's a bad feeling. 

Finally, the updates are too far between and under deliver. The main QoL changes are missing a year after the release of the game. A single career takes an hour to complete, that's a lot to ask of people with missing features like spark rerolls and affinity changes (just announced.) Not even super skip to alleviate MANT time sink or auto career to maintain account when taking a break.

If this is your only game and only thing you do in life, then maybe I can recommend it. If you value your time, stay away. Cygames does not respect their players.

(Updated July 25, 2026)

[h1] Positives [/h1]
[list]
[*]Designs: Very recognizable and allows players to identify other Umas from a quick glance during a race.
[*]Story: Individual Uma stories in a Career run are enjoyable to read. Stories from Events are also enjoyable as those tend to feature great fullscreen art and fun character interactions.
[*]Non-Competitive: There isn't much competitive aspects in the game beyond Team Trials or the monthly Champions Meetings, both of which aren't of any significant importance beyond completing for Dailies/Carats.  
[*]Carats: The game is quite generous with Carat distribution as it can be obtained from a multitude of different avenues where someone can obtain the necessary amount for a pity pull (30,000).
[*]Tickets: The Ticket system is fantastic as Tickets are awarded during Events or redeemed from various Shop menus which can be used in banner pulls and would be used first instead of your Carats, only issue I have with it is it can't be used in bulk of x10 use so it's a slow wait of having to spend Tickets one-by-one.
[*]Gacha: The gacha aspect is quite fun and forgiving. When reaching Pity pull, the game will allow the player to outright choose which spotlight/featured banner Uma or Skill Card. Also when pulling, your pulls may randomly be 'upgraded' and increase in Rarity, and in extremely lucky instances you can have a basic pull be 'upgraded' to SSR.
[*]Auto-Mode: The addition of Auto-mode allows users to do a career run for a Scenario of their choice which will complete itself in 50 minutes. While there are drawbacks to using this feature that may not be ideal for more experienced players, it does allow those who aren't as engaged in the deeper mechanics or lack the time to do a run to get their dailies done which I do appreciate is given to players.
[/list]

If you are fine with all of that, Umamusume also has a lot of fun and other stories for each character and scenario to occupy your time. As someone playing for... almost a year now, I wouldn't recommend this game, but feel free to give it a try, it is free.

It's been a year since I've seen that one gif of Gold Ship's G1 victory animation and started playing the game, and it still has me hooked. The gameplay loop can get stale at times but it still has me coming back every day. I love reading through every trainee's careers and seeing them grow to overcome their challenges, with some actually coming close to bringing me to tears. That's just how good the writing and music are able to pull of some emotional moments. 

My only complaints is that the gacha aspect isn't that good, which is a given in gacha games, and it's really hard to recommend the game to people, as the game is gets less and less beginner-friendly as time goes on. The only real way for beginners to get into Umamusume is by paying a ton of money to catch up to the players who started earlier than them, which still isn't enough as anyone can also pay money to get good trainees and support cards to get better Umas.

Other than those complaints, Umamusume is an addictive game with heartwarming stories that give the respect and recognition the real racehorses deserve and I'm glad I've started playing it a year ago.

claims.claim: Completing a single career run takes between one to three hours.

citations.review_text: Just another game you'll wish you could quit but can't bring yourself to (victim of the sunk cost fallacy). Accellerated timeline on global leaves little breathing room between PVP events. You CAN have fun without following the meta as it can be experimental and there is a lot of wiggleroom for constructing your own builds to counter / compete, however whales have a massive advantage due to how the pull system works. ON THAT NOTE, incredibly unforgiving, nothing carries over between pulls, it's a fresh start everytime. That being said, F2P players can enjoy a lot of story and the gameplay loop can be incredibly addictive and rewarding IF YOU HAVE THE TIME FOR IT, currently it takes me 2-3 hours to do all three of the career runs you're given per day. That being said, I will continue playing. You have been warned.

I would recommend the game to casual players who enjoy VN and interesting characters. They did a good job with the story and the accelerated schedule is a huge plus since there is always something new.

However

The game is very predatory. You either spend hundreds of dollars for ONE fully unlocked card or you spend months saving free currency, skipping every single banner. The pity system is brutal, the RNG is brutal, and you can spend dozens of hours or even days and weeks grinding with 0 progress to your account. The game forces you to grind more and more for incremental gains if you're lucky just to MAYBE win the monthly pvp mode. It's a bad feeling. 

Finally, the updates are too far between and under deliver. The main QoL changes are missing a year after the release of the game. A single career takes an hour to complete, that's a lot to ask of people with missing features like spark rerolls and affinity changes (just announced.) Not even super skip to alleviate MANT time sink or auto career to maintain account when taking a break.

If this is your only game and only thing you do in life, then maybe I can recommend it. If you value your time, stay away. Cygames does not respect their players.

No do not play this game if you are trying to make the "Best horse girl"
Play this game only if you like the characters and school story setting.

TRACKBLAZER has been utter waste zone of agony. Runs went from a nice 20 minutes to with MANT averaging 40minutes to 1 hour runs because of load times. WITHOUT cheating might I add.

Getting a 1 blue spark and 1 pink spark for your uma parent after a fantastic run makes you want to quit every time once you learn the mechanics of the actual gaame.

I don't this the new scenario will make many improvements for this. So until they have Auto play function if you are a casual player you usually have a very very slim chance to compete against other players in the "PVP" modes. The PVP modes are the whole point to show off your trained UMA to other players.

There are two types of players. I love training my favorite Uma. As a gacha game, getting some Umas or uncapping strong meta support cards can be difficult. You need carrots and a bit of luck. However, the RNG makes the game interesting as long as you don't take it too seriously.

Unfortunately, some cheaters have appeared, creating Umas with impossible fan counts and an unrealistic number of gold skills. That's the part I hate also one career run takes me about an hour to compete in the new escenario. I'm looking forward to the new scenario when it comes out.

I really like the character designs, the game modes, and the characters. The game is fun, and it's easy to relate to and become attached to them. I also enjoy the horse racing fandom.

[h1] Positives [/h1]
[list]
[*]Designs: Very recognizable and allows players to identify other Umas from a quick glance during a race.
[*]Story: Individual Uma stories in a Career run are enjoyable to read. Stories from Events are also enjoyable as those tend to feature great fullscreen art and fun character interactions.
[*]Non-Competitive: There isn't much competitive aspects in the game beyond Team Trials or the monthly Champions Meetings, both of which aren't of any significant importance beyond completing for Dailies/Carats.  
[*]Carats: The game is quite generous with Carat distribution as it can be obtained from a multitude of different avenues where someone can obtain the necessary amount for a pity pull (30,000).
[*]Tickets: The Ticket system is fantastic as Tickets are awarded during Events or redeemed from various Shop menus which can be used in banner pulls and would be used first instead of your Carats, only issue I have with it is it can't be used in bulk of x10 use so it's a slow wait of having to spend Tickets one-by-one.
[*]Gacha: The gacha aspect is quite fun and forgiving. When reaching Pity pull, the game will allow the player to outright choose which spotlight/featured banner Uma or Skill Card. Also when pulling, your pulls may randomly be 'upgraded' and increase in Rarity, and in extremely lucky instances you can have a basic pull be 'upgraded' to SSR.
[*]Auto-Mode: The addition of Auto-mode allows users to do a career run for a Scenario of their choice which will complete itself in 50 minutes. While there are drawbacks to using this feature that may not be ideal for more experienced players, it does allow those who aren't as engaged in the deeper mechanics or lack the time to do a run to get their dailies done which I do appreciate is given to players.
[/list]
